subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group chats get first-class opt-in dynamic per-sender agents, or should OpenClaw keep sender-scoped group sessions plus explicit subagent/thread commands as the supported isolation model?
rationale: Current source has partial session and subagent infrastructure, but the requested architecture changes channel routing, agent lifecycle, memory isolation, skills, config writes, resource limits, and security boundaries.

options.title: Design Opt-In Group Sender Agents
options.body: Use this issue as the umbrella decision, then split approved work into Feishu plugin routing, memory/skill policy, lifecycle limits, admin authorization, docs, and live-proof tasks.

options.title: Keep Session Scopes Only
options.body: Treat group_sender and group_topic_sender as the supported isolation contract and close or rewrite the automatic subagent parts as out of scope.

options.title: Defer To Narrower API Work
options.body: Resolve account-scoped group sessions, plain-group binding, channel threading policy, and user skill preferences before revisiting automatic Feishu group subagents.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Group Sender Agents
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the umbrella decision, then split approved work into Feishu plugin routing, memory/skill policy, lifecycle limits, admin authorization, docs, and live-proof tasks.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-main history signal across Feishu group session routing and dynamic-agent behavior.
